notes: No box-shadow anywhere (Flat-Ledger Rule). Depth is hairlines + tonal washes only.
No @media breakpoints; layout is a single 1100px-max column. The viewport meta is set; responsiveness comes from fluid tables, not breakpoints.
No prefers-reduced-motion handling exists yet; add it before introducing any new motion.
Background/text are CSS system colors (Canvas/CanvasText), so the report follows the OS light/dark theme; do not hardcode them.

components.name: Data Table

components.css: .ds-table { border-collapse: collapse; width: 100%; font: 0.92rem/1.5 -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", Roboto, sans-serif; } .ds-table th, .ds-table td { text-align: left; padding: 0.45rem 0.6rem; border-bottom: 1px solid #88888844; vertical-align: top; } .ds-table th { font-weight: 600; border-bottom: 2px solid #88888866; } .ds-table .num { text-align: right; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; } .ds-table tr:hover td { background: #88888811; } .ds-table .mono { font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, monospace; font-size: 0.85rem; }

narrative.overview: agent-census renders one thing: a plain-paper investigator's record where every observation is logged and every verdict is defensible from the entry sitting next to it. No app shell, no nav, no hero, no cards-as-decoration — a stack of dense, scannable tables on the bare substrate of the OS's own light or dark surface, read top-to-bottom like a ledger. The aesthetic is unstyled on purpose; what little visual force the page spends, it spends on meaning. Built on three constraints, each a feature: one file with zero dependencies (opens from file://, renders identically in ten years); deference to the OS (Canvas/CanvasText + a single adaptive gray, legible in light and dark with no toggle); and a hard line between claim and finding (client-asserted strings in monospace, the report's own prose and verdicts in system sans).
keyCharacteristics: Flat. No shadows anywhere; depth is hairlines and tonal washes only.
System-native: OS light/dark substrate, system font stack, zero assets.
Dense by intent — tables run wide and long; the operator wants the data.
Color is a legend, never decoration. Every hue is a documented fact.
Mono = claim, sans = finding. The two are never visually merged.
Single, self-contained HTML file; portability is non-negotiable.

rules.name: The System-Color Substrate Rule
rules.body: Background and body text are Canvas and CanvasText; structural grays are #888 + alpha. Never replace them with fixed hex — it breaks dark mode and the zero-config promise.

rules.name: The Meaning-Only Color Rule
rules.body: Every non-neutral hue is in the legend and stands for a fact (a kind, a verdict, an egress type). If a color isn't encoding one of those, it does not belong on the page.

rules.name: The White-On-Hue Rule
rules.body: Any chip filled with a palette hue carries #ffffff text. Unsignalled tags stay on the neutral #88888833 track with inherited CanvasText.

rules.name: The Claim-in-Mono Rule
rules.body: Anything the client asserted (IP, User-Agent, requested paths) is set in monospace; the report's own narration and verdicts are set in the system sans. The typeface boundary is the boundary between what the log said and what agent-census concluded.

rules.name: The One-Family Rule
rules.body: The system sans carries every structural role. No display face, no second sans, no brand font. Mono is the only permitted second family, and only for verbatim strings.

rules.name: The Flat-Ledger Rule
rules.body: No box-shadow, ever — not on cards, not on hover, not on the sticky filter. Separation uses a hairline or tonal wash; emphasis uses weight or color-heat.

dos: Do keep background and body text on Canvas / CanvasText and structural lines on #888 + alpha, so the single file stays legible in both OS themes.
Do treat color as a legend: every non-neutral hue must map to a kind, a verdict, or an egress type documented in the Colors section.
Do set every client-asserted string (IP, UA, path, client id) in monospace and every report finding in the system sans — preserve the Claim-in-Mono Rule.
Do give colored chips #ffffff text and leave unsignalled tags on the neutral #88888833 track.
Do convey depth and grouping with hairlines and tonal washes; convey magnitude with the share bar or variable-alpha heat.
Do keep tables dense — they may exceed prose line-length; use tabular-nums on numeric columns.
Do give any future motion a prefers-reduced-motion: reduce fallback; the only motion today is the 120ms triangle rotation and the copy flash.
donts: Don't ship marketing-dashboard slop — no hero-metric tiles, no gradients, no glassmorphism, no identical icon-and-heading card grids.
Don't ship SOC / security-vendor theatrics — no alarm-red everywhere, no fake threat-level gauges, no dark-cyber cosplay. Red is reserved for documented hostile-conduct signals.
Don't ship over-chromed enterprise BI — no 3-D bars, no skeuomorphic gauges, no decorative chartjunk.
Don't add a box-shadow anywhere — the Flat-Ledger Rule is absolute.
Don't hardcode a background or text hex; never break the System-Color Substrate Rule.
Don't introduce a web font, a display face, or a second sans. One system sans plus mono, nothing more.
Don't use color as decoration, render a finding in mono, or set a raw claim in sans.
Don't add external assets (fonts, images, CSS/JS files). The report is one self-contained file and must stay that way.
